'''David Tománek''' (born July 1954) is a U.S.-Swiss physicist of Czech origin and researcher in [[nanoscience]] and [[nanotechnology]]. He is Emeritus Professor of Physics at Michigan State University.  He is known for predicting the structure and calculating properties of [[Surface science|surfaces]], [[atomic clusters]] including the C<sub>60</sub> [[buckminsterfullerene]], [[nanotubes]],<ref name="NYT-CNT">{{cite news |title=New York Times: Of nanotubes and buckyballs |work=The New York Times |date=27 March 2001 |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2001/03/27/science/of-nanotubes-and-buckyballs-atomic-scale-building-blocks.html|last1=Chang |first1=Kenneth }}</ref> [[nanowires]] and [[helices|nanohelices]],<ref name="Helix">{{cite news |title=Advances in Engineering: Origin of Unusually High Rigidity in Selected Helical Coil Structures |url=https://advanceseng.com/origin-unusually-high-rigidity-helical-coil-structures/}}</ref> [[graphene]],<ref name="PRF">{{cite news |title=Physical Review Focus: Diamonds Aren't Forever |url=https://physics.aps.org/story/v22/st5}}</ref> and [[two-dimensional materials]] including [[phosphorene]].<ref name="Nat-P">{{cite news |title=Nature: Phosphorene excites materials scientists |url=https://www.nature.com/news/phosphorene-excites-materials-scientists-1.14668}}</ref><ref name="Sci-P">{{cite news |title=Science News: Phosphorene introduced as graphene alternative |url=https://www.sciencenews.org/article/phosphorene-introduced-graphene-alternative}}</ref>

== Academic career ==
Tománek earned a [[doctoral]] degree in [[Physics]] from the [[Freie Universität Berlin]] in 1983 under the supervision of [[Karl Heinz Bennemann]] and became Hochschulassistent there in 1984.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=David Tománek's C.V.|url=https://nanoten.com/tomanek/vita.html|access-date=October 5, 2020|website=Computational Nanotechnology Lab at Michigan State University.}}</ref> Between 1985 and 1987 he worked as [[postdoctoral researcher]] at the [[Bell Labs]]<ref name=":0" /> under the supervision of Michael A. Schlüter and at the [[University of California, Berkeley]] under the supervision of [[Steven Gwon Sheng Louie|Steven G. Louie]]. Since 1987, he has been Professor of Physics at [[Michigan State University]], where he directs the Computational Nanotechnology Laboratory<ref name="CNL">{{cite web |title=Computational Nanotechnology Laboratory |url=https://nanoten.com/tomanek/CNL.html}}</ref> at the Department of Physics and Astronomy.<ref name="MSU-PA">{{cite web |title=MSU Department of Physics and Astronomy |url=https://pa.msu.edu/}}</ref><ref name=":0" />

== Research ==
Tománek and his research group have worked in areas in [[nanoscience]] and [[nanotechnology]]. As a graduate student at [[FU Berlin]], he studied structural end electronic properties of [[Surface science|surfaces]], including [[Surface reconstruction|reconstruction]] and photoemission spectra. He was intrigued by the unusual structure and electronic properties of [[atomic clusters]],<ref name="DT010">{{cite journal |last1=Tomanek |first1=D |last2=Mukherjee |first2=S |last3=Bennemann |first3=KH |title=Simple theory for the electronic and atomic structure of small clusters |journal=Phys. Rev. B |date=1983 |volume=28 |issue=2 |pages=665–673 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevB.28.665|bibcode=1983PhRvB..28..665T }}</ref><ref name="DT010e">{{cite journal |last1=Tomanek |first1=D |last2=Mukherjee |first2=S |last3=Bennemann |first3=KH |title=Erratum: Simple theory for the electronic and atomic structure of small clusters |journal=Phys. Rev. B |date=1984 |volume=29 |issue=2 |page=1076 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevB.28.665|bibcode=1983PhRvB..28..665T }}</ref> including collective electronic excitations<ref name="DT052">{{cite journal |last1=Bertsch |first1=George F. |last2=Bulgac |first2=Aurel |last3=Tomanek |first3=David |last4=Wang |first4=Yang |title=Collective plasmon excitations in C<sub>60</sub> clusters |journal=Phys. Rev. Lett. |date=1991 |volume=67 |issue=19 |pages=2690–2693 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.67.2690|pmid=10044492 |bibcode=1991PhRvL..67.2690B }}</ref> and superconductivity.<ref name="DT053">{{cite journal |last1=Schluter |first1=M |last2=Lannoo |first2=M |last3=Needels |first3=M  |last4=Baraff |first4=GA |last5=Tomanek |first5=D |title=Electron-phonon coupling and superconductivity in alkali-intercalated C<sub>60</sub> solid |journal=Phys. Rev. Lett. |date=1992  |volume=68  |issue=4  |pages=526–529 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.68.526|pmid=10045919 |bibcode=1992PhRvL..68..526S }}</ref> His computational studies of growth regimes of silicon<ref name="DT">{{cite journal |last1=Tomanek |first1=D. |last2=Schlüter |first2=M A |title=Calculation of magic numbers and the stability of small Si clusters |journal=Phys. Rev. Lett. |date=1986 |volume=56 |issue=10 |pages=1055–1058 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.56.1055|pmid=10032556 |bibcode=1986PhRvL..56.1055T }}</ref> and carbon<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Tomanek |first1=David |last2=Schluter |first2=Michael A. |title=Growth regimes of carbon clusters |journal=Phys. Rev. Lett. |date=1991 |volume=67 |issue=17 |pages=2331–2334 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.67.2331|pmid=10044399 |bibcode=1991PhRvL..67.2331T }}</ref> clusters have made use of the semi-quantitative [[Linear combination of atomic orbitals|Linear Combination of Atomic Orbitals]] (LCAO) or [[tight-binding]] method.<ref name=":0" />

During his 1994 [[sabbatical]] stay at the laboratory of [[Richard E. Smalley]], he turned his interest to the unique properties of [[nanotubes]] formed of [[carbon nanotubes|carbon (CNTs)]] and other materials. == Conferences ==
Tománek initiated a series of annual Nanotube (NT) conferences<ref name=":0" /> and a [[Gordon Research Conference]] on ''Two-dimensional electronics beyond graphene.''<ref name="GRC-2D">{{cite web |title=Gordon Research Conference: Two-dimensional electronics beyond graphene |url=https://www.grc.org/two-dimensional-electronics-beyond-graphene-conference/2016/}}</ref>

== Honors and awards ==
In 2004 Tománek was elected a Fellow of the [[American Physical Society]]<ref name="APSfellow">{{cite web |last1=American Physical Society Fellows |title=David Tomanek becomes APS fellow in 2004 |url=https://www.aps.org/units/dmp/fellowship/index.cfm?year=2004 |access-date=26 March 2020}}</ref> and in 2005 he received the prestigious Alexander-von-Humboldt Senior Scientist Award<ref name="AvH">{{cite web |title=Alexander-von-Humboldt Senior Scientist Award |url=https://www.humboldt-foundation.de/web/humboldt-award.html}}</ref> (Germany). In 2008 he received the Japan Carbon Award for Life-Time Achievement and was chosen by the [[American Physical Society]] as member of the Outstanding Referees Program<ref name="APS-ref">{{cite web |title=APS Outstanding Referees program |url=http://journals.aps.org/OutstandingReferees}}</ref> for excellence in peer review. In 2016 he received the Lee Hsun Research Award for Materials Science<ref name="Lee Hsun">{{cite web |title=Lee Hsun Research Award for Materials Science |url=http://english.imr.cas.cn/news/newsrelease/201506/t20150615_148878.html}}</ref> from the [[Chinese Academy of Sciences]]. His [[h-index]] is currently 85.<ref name="Google-scholar">{{cite web |title=Google scholar record of David Tomanek |url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?hl=en&user=LYfhKXEAAAAJ |access-date=29 March 2020}}</ref>
